# ==============================================================================
# .github/allowed-files.txt
#
# Explicit, reviewed exceptions to scripts/checks/check-forbidden-files.sh.
#
# Every line is a path or a glob matched against the repository-relative path
# of a file tracked by git. Blank lines and lines starting with '#' are ignored.
#
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
#   A hard "never commit this" list is only trustworthy if the exceptions to it
#   are as visible as the rule itself. Adding an exception here shows up in the
#   pull request diff, is covered by CODEOWNERS, and forces a human to write down
#   why the file is needed. Editing the glob list inside the check script to
#   make a build go green is exactly the failure mode this file prevents.
#
# RULES FOR MAINTAINERS
#   * One entry per line, most specific first.
#   * Add a comment explaining the exception.
#   * If the exception is temporary, say when it expires.
#   * If you cannot justify it in one sentence, the file does not belong in git.
# ==============================================================================

# --- Brand assets -------------------------------------------------------------
# The club logo is a legitimate, small, versioned binary asset. It is the only
# binary the repository is expected to contain until real media is needed.
# (Kept for documentation; it is already under the 1 MiB limit, so the check
# passes without this entry.)
# public/assets/brand/logo.png

# --- Example environment template --------------------------------------------
# The ONLY environment file that may be committed. It documents the required
# variables and must never contain a real value — CI scans it for secrets.
# .env.example
# .env.template

# --- Vendored, intentionally committed third-party code -----------------------
# Add entries here only with CODEOWNERS approval, and prefer adding the
# dependency to package.json over vendoring it.
# src/vendor/

# --- Legal / institutional documents ------------------------------------------
# Files the club is contractually required to keep in the repository.
# docs/legal/
